h: חַג הַפֶּסַח, מַאֲמָר כ׳ Pesach — Maamar Kaf
A Night of Watchfulness: Hu, the Hidden Light and Pesach's Two Holinesses

p: בַּזֹּהַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ
In the holy Zohar
(חֵלֶק ב' ל"ח.):
וְתָנָא: הֲוָה נָהִיר לֵילְיָא כְּיוֹמָא דִּתְקוּפַת תַּמּוּז וְכוּלֵּי.
"And it was taught: That night [of the Exodus] shone like the day of the summer solstice of Tammuz, etc."
וְלֹא נִתְפָּרֵשׁ בַּזֹּהַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ מְנָא לֵיהּ זֶה,
Now it is not explicitly stated in the holy Zohar from where it derives this,
אַךְ נִרְאֶה דִּמְדַיֵּיק מִלְּשׁוֹן הַכָּתוּב
yet it appears that it infers it from the wording of the verse
(שְׁמוֹת י"ב, מ"ב):
(Shemos 12:42):
לֵיל שִׁמֻּרִים הוּא לַה' וְגוֹמֵר הוּא הַלַּיְלָה הַזֶּה וְגוֹמֵר
"It is a night of watchfulness (leil shimurim hu) for Hashem, etc., this is that night (hu ha'lailah ha'zeh), etc."
וְאֵין לְשׁוֹן "הוּא" מִתְפָּרֵשׁ כָּאן, וּבִפְרָט לְשׁוֹן "הוּא הַלַּיְלָה הַזֶּה".
for the word hu ("he/it") is otherwise unexplained here, and especially the phrase "He is this night."
וְאַחַר כָּךְ מְדַיֵּיק בַּזֹּהַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ:
And afterward the holy Zohar infers:
כֵּיוָן דְּאָמַר "לֵיל", מַהוּ "שִׁמֻּרִים" וְלֹא "שָׁמוּר" וְכוּלֵּי, "לֵיל" קָאָמַר בְּקַדְמֵיתָא וּלְבָתַר "לַיְלָה" וְכוּלֵּי;
"Since it says leil (singular), why does it say shimurim (plural) rather than shamur, etc., and why does it say leil at first and afterward lailah, etc.?"
וְאָמַר בַּזֹּהַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ:
And the holy Zohar explains:
"לֵיל" עַד דְּלָא קַבִּילַת דְּכַר וְכוּלֵּי,
"Leil refers to before [the feminine Shechinah] received the masculine aspect, etc.,
וּבְשַׁעְתָּא דְּאִתְחַבַּר עִמָּהּ דְּכַר: הוּא הַלַּיְלָה הַזֶּה לַה', שִׁמֻּרִים — דְּכַר וְנוּקְבָא וְכוּלֵּי,
and at the moment the masculine aspect united with her, 'He is this night for Hashem, shimurim'—both masculine and feminine, etc.
וּבַאֲתַר דְּאִשְׁתַּכְּחוּ דְּכַר וְנוּקְבָא לֵית שְׁבָחָא אֶלָּא לִדְכוּרָא וְכוּלֵּי
and in a place where masculine and feminine are found together, praise is given solely to the masculine, etc."
וּמִתְפָּרֵשׁ מַה שֶּׁנֶּאֱמַר: הַלַּיְלָה הַזֶּה שִׁמֻּרִים.
which explains why it says "this night is shimurim."
אַךְ לָמָּה נִזְכַּר "הוּא הַלַּיְלָה הַזֶּה"?
Yet why is it stated "Hu (He) is this night"?
וּמִזֶּה מְדַיֵּיק הַזֹּהַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ דַּהֲוָה נָהִיר לֵילְיָא כְּיוֹמָא דִּתְקוּפַת תַּמּוּז,
From this the holy Zohar infers that the night shone like the day of the summer solstice of Tammuz,
שֶׁבְּכָל מָקוֹם נִקְרָא שֵׂכֶל הַנֶּעְלָם מִכָּל רַעְיוֹן "הוּא":
for everywhere the Supernal Intellect concealed from all human thought is called Hu ("He"):
אַתָּה הוּא עַד שֶׁלֹּא נִבְרָא הָעוֹלָם וְכוּלֵּי,
"You are Hu before the world was created, etc.,"
וְכֵן לֶעָתִיד נִקְרָא "יוֹם הַהוּא", שֶׁאָז יִתְגַּלֶּה אוֹר הַנִּקְרָא "הוּא".
and likewise the future is called "that day" (Yom HaHu), when the light called Hu will be revealed.
וְזֶה שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר:
And this is what is said:
וַיְהִי בְּעֶצֶם הַיּוֹם הַזֶּה יָצְאוּ וְגוֹמֵר,
"And it came to pass on this very day (b'etzem ha'yom ha'zeh), they went out, etc."
וּמְפָרֵשׁ הַפָּסוּק שֶׁלְּאַחֲרָיו לָמָּה נִקְרָא הַיּוֹם "עֶצֶם הַיּוֹם הַזֶּה", שֶׁפֵּירוּשׁוֹ זְרִיחַת אוֹר הַגָּנוּז שֶׁיִּהְיֶה לוֹ בּוֹ תְּפִיסָה:
and the very next verse explains why the day is called "this very day"—meaning the shining forth of the hidden primordial light such that one can grasp it
לֵיל שִׁמֻּרִים הוּא לַה',
"It is a night of watchfulness (Hu) for Hashem":
שֶׁבְּלַיְלָה זֹאת נִתְגַּלָּה לָהֶם מֵאוֹר הַגָּנוּז שֶׁמַּאֲמַר יְהִי אוֹר יִהְיֶה בּוֹ תְּפִיסָה,
because on that night there was revealed to them a ray of the hidden light from the utterance "Let there be light" in a graspable manner,
וְזֶה שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר "הוּא הַלַּיְלָה הַזֶּה"
and this is what is meant by "Hu is this night"
"זֶה" מוֹרֶה שֶׁיֵּשׁ בּוֹ תְּפִיסָה שֶׁמּוֹרֶה בְּאֶצְבַּע כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמַרְנוּ,
"this" (zeh) indicates that it is graspable, something one can point to with a finger, as we have explained,
וְנִקְרָא "שִׁמֻּרִים", דְּכַר הֲוָה זְמִין לְאִתְחַבְּרָא עִמָּהּ,
and it is called shimurim, for the masculine aspect was prepared to unite with her,
וְאַחַר כָּךְ כְּשֶׁיֵּשׁ זִיוּוּגָא נִקְרָא: הַלַּיְלָה הַזֶּה לַה', דְּלֵית שְׁבָחָא אֶלָּא לִדְכוּרָא;
and afterward when there is union it is called "this night for Hashem," for praise belongs solely to the masculine;
וּבְגִין כָּךְ כְּתִיב: הוּא הַלַּיְלָה הַזֶּה, שֶׁהָיָה הוֹפָעָה מִכֶּתֶר עֶלְיוֹן שֶׁנִּקְרָא "הוּא".
and therefore it is written "Hu is this night," because there was an illumination from Kesser Elyon, which is called Hu.
וּמִטַּעַם זֶה נִקְרָא הֲנָפַת הָעוֹמֶר "מִמָּחֳרַת הַשַּׁבָּת" סְתָם,
And for this reason the waving of the Omer is called "the morrow of the Shabbos" without qualification,
דִּבְשַׁבָּת יֵשׁ בּוֹ הִתְגַּלּוּת עַתִּיקָא, וּמִטַּעַם זֶה אוֹמְרִים קְדוּשַּׁת כֶּתֶר,
for on Shabbos there is a revelation of Atika, which is why we recite the Kedushah of Kesser [in Musaf],
דִּבְכָל מָקוֹם שֶׁיֵּשׁ זִיוּוּג יֵשׁ גַּם כֵּן הִתְגַּלּוּת עַתִּיקָא, וּכְמוֹ שֶׁמּוּבָא בַּזֹּהַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ
since wherever there is supernal union there is also a revelation of Atika, as brought in the holy Zohar
(חֵלֶק ג' ע"ט:):
דְּהָא עַתִּיקָא אִתְגְּלֵי וְזִיוּוּגָא יִזְדַּמֵּן וְכוּלֵּי.
"For behold, Atika is revealed and union is prepared, etc."
וְנִזְכַּר לֵיל שִׁמֻּרִים שֶׁמִּזֶּה הוֹפִיעַ הַקְּדוּשָּׁה לֶחָג, כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמַרְנוּ בְּמַה שֶּׁנֶּאֱמַר: כְּלֵיל הִתְקַדֶּשׁ חָג
And "night of watchfulness" is mentioned because from it holiness shone forth to the entire festival, as we explained regarding the verse "as on the night when the festival is sanctified"
(מַאֲמָר ט"ז).
(Maamar 16).
וְנִקְרָא גַּם יוֹם הֲנָפַת הָעוֹמֶר "עֶצֶם הַיּוֹם הַזֶּה", שֶׁיֵּשׁ בּוֹ גַּם כֵּן הִתְגַּלּוּת מֵאוֹר הַגָּנוּז.
And the day of waving the Omer is also called "this very day" (etzem ha'yom ha'zeh), because it too contains a revelation of the hidden primordial light.
וְלָכֵן הַחֲכָמִים בְּתוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה שֶׁהִיא מִטַּלָּא דְּעַתִּיקָא,
Therefore, the Sages of the Oral Torah—which emanates from the Dew of Atika
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר
as it is said
(אִיּוֹב כ"ח, י'):
כָּל יְקָר רָאֲתָה עֵינוֹ
"His eye saw every precious thing"
רָאֲתָה עֵינוֹ שֶׁל רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא וַחֲבֵירָיו מַה שֶּׁלֹּא רָאָה מֹשֶׁה
the eye of Rabbi Akiva and his colleagues saw what Moshe did not see
(בְּמִדְבַּר רַבָּה י"ט, ו' וְתַנְחוּמָא חֻקַּת ח')
(Bamidbar Rabbah 19:6 and Tanchuma Chukas 8)
הֵם יָכְלוּ לְצָרֵף שְׁנֵי הָאוֹרוֹת: "עֶצֶם הַיּוֹם הַזֶּה" שֶׁל יוֹם טוֹב דְּפֶסַח, וְ"עֶצֶם הַיּוֹם הַזֶּה" שֶׁל הֲנָפַת הָעוֹמֶר בְּיַחַד,
they were able to combine both lights together: "this very day" of the festival of Pesach and "this very day" of the waving of the Omer,
אַף שֶׁהֵם תַּרְתֵּי דְּסָתְרֵי: שֶׁמְּבָרְכִין עַל אֲכִילַת מַצָּה וּמָרוֹר וְאוֹמְרִים הַלֵּל וְסוֹפְרִין סְפִירַת הָעוֹמֶר.

even though they appear to be two contradictory things: reciting blessings over eating matzah and maror and saying full Hallel [as on the first day of Yom Tov], while simultaneously counting Sefiras HaOmer [as on Chol HaMoed].

אַךְ עַל פִּי הָאָמוּר בְּ"עֶצֶם הַיּוֹם הַזֶּה" מוֹרֶה הִתְגַּלּוּת הָאוֹר הַגָּנוּז שֶׁנִּקְרָא "יוֹם", שֶׁיִּהְיֶה בּוֹ תְּפִיסָה, וְהוּא עַל יְדֵי הִתְגַּלּוּת מִכֶּתֶר עֶלְיוֹן שֶׁנִּקְרָא "הוּא",

Yet according to what we explained, "this very day" signifies the revelation of the hidden primordial light called "Day" in a graspable manner, which occurs through a revelation from Kesser Elyon called Hu,

וּבְעַתִּיקָא שֶׁהוּא לְמַעְלָה מֵהַזְּמַן אֵין שׁוּם סְתִירָה, וְיָכוֹל לִהְיוֹת שְׁתֵּי הַקְּדוּשּׁוֹת—קְדוּשַּׁת "עֶצֶם הַיּוֹם הַזֶּה" הַנִּזְכָּר בִּיצִיאַת מִצְרַיִם וּקְדוּשַּׁת "עֶצֶם הַיּוֹם הַזֶּה" הַנִּזְכָּר בְּיוֹם הֲנָפַת הָעוֹמֶר—בְּיַחַד

and in Atika, which transcends time, there is no contradiction whatsoever, so both holinesses—the holiness of "this very day" mentioned at the Exodus and the holiness of "this very day" mentioned on the day of waving the Omer—can coexist together
(כְּמוֹ שֶׁנִּתְבָּאֵר מַאֲמָר י"ז).
(as explained in Maamar 17).
וְאָמַר: שִׁמֻּרִים לְכָל בְּנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל לְדֹרֹתָם
And the verse states: "watchfulness for all the Children of Israel throughout their generations"
שֶׁחַיָּיב אָדָם לִרְאוֹת אֶת עַצְמוֹ כְּאִילּוּ הוּא יָצָא מִמִּצְרַיִם,
for a person is obligated to view himself as though he personally went out of Egypt,
וּבְכָל לֵיל פֶּסַח צָרִיךְ שֶׁיַּרְגִּישׁ שִׁינּוּי וְאוֹר חָדָשׁ כְּמוֹ בְּעֵת יְצִיאַת מִצְרַיִם,
and on every Pesach night one must experience a transformation and a new light just as at the time of the Exodus from Egypt,
וּמִזֶּה מוֹפִיעַ הַקְּדוּשָּׁה לְכָל הֶחָג וּלְכָל הַמּוֹעֲדִים הַבָּאִים, שֶׁרֶגֶל זֶה רֹאשׁ הַשָּׁנָה לָרְגָלִים, כְּמוֹ שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר
and from this, holiness shines forth to the entire festival and to all subsequent festivals, since this festival is the New Year for the pilgrimage festivals, as it is said
(יְשַׁעְיָה ל', כ"ט):
(Yeshayahu 30:29):
הַשִּׁיר יִהְיֶה לָכֶם כְּלֵיל הִתְקַדֶּשׁ חָג.
"You shall have a song as on the night when a festival is sanctified."
וְכֵן מָצִינוּ בַּגְּמָרָא
And so we find in the Gemara
(פְּסָחִים פ"ה:):
(Pesachim 85b):
כְּזַיְתָא פִּסְחָא וְהַלֵּילָא פָּקַע אִיגְּרָא
"An olive's bulk of the Pesach offering, and the Hallel splits the roof"
וְהַיְינוּ שֶׁבִּשְׁעַת הַהַלֵּל נִפְתַּח הָאוֹר כְּמוֹ שֶׁנִּפְקַע הָאִיגְּרָא וְנִתְבַּקְּעוּ הַגַּגִּין וְנִתְגַּלָּה עֶצֶם הַשָּׁמַיִם לָטֹהַר,
meaning that during the recitation of Hallel the supernal light opens up as though the roof split apart and the heavens themselves were revealed in their purity,
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁמָּצִינוּ
and as we find
(בְּרָכוֹת מ"ח.):
(Berachos 48a):
וְרַחֲמָנָא הֵיכִי יָתֵיב? רָבָא אַחְוִי לִשְׁמֵי טַלָּלָא, אַבַּיֵּי נָפֵיק לְבָרָא אַחְוִי כְּלַפֵּי שְׁמַיָּא
"'And where does the Merciful One dwell?' Rava pointed upward toward the ceiling, while Abaye went outside and pointed toward the heavens"
שֶׁאַבַּיֵּי הָיָה לוֹ הֲבָנָה שֶׁצָּרִיךְ לֵילֵךְ לַחוּץ שֶׁלֹּא יִהְיֶה הֶפְסֵק הַגַּג,
for Abaye understood that one must go outside so that the roof does not interpose,
וְכֵן כָּאן הַלָּשׁוֹן "פָּקַע אִיגְּרָא" שֶׁנִּתְגַּלָּה הָאוֹר בְּעֵת קְרִיאַת הַהַלֵּל שֶׁלֹּא הָיָה שׁוּם הֶבְדֵּל, כְּאִילּוּ הַגַּגִּין נִתְבַּקְּעוּ.
and similarly here the phrase "splits the roof" means that the supernal light was revealed during Hallel with no barrier whatsoever, as though the roofs were split open.
וַחֲכָמִים הָיָה בְּכֹחָם לְצָרֵף שְׁתֵּי הַקְּדוּשּׁוֹת יַחַד, כֵּיוָן שֶׁשְּׁנֵיהֶם נִקְרָאִים "עֶצֶם הַיּוֹם הַזֶּה" שֶׁהוּא הִתְגַּלּוּת אוֹר הַגָּנוּז,
And the Sages had the power to combine both holinesses together, since both are called "this very day," which is the revelation of the hidden primordial light,
וּבְעַתִּיקָא אֵין שׁוּם סְתִירָה מֵהַזְּמַן, שֶׁהוּא לְמַעְלָה מֵהַזְּמַן וְיָכוֹל לִהְיוֹת שְׁתֵּי הַקְּדוּשּׁוֹת יַחַד.
and in Atika there is no contradiction from time, since it transcends time and both holinesses can coexist together.

paragraphs.text: Zohar II 38a (Bo) — "Judgment was carried out on all at the hour when they had all gathered into their houses… and the night carried out its judgments on all at that hour. And it was taught: that night shone like the day at the Tammuz solstice, and all the people saw the judgments of the Holy One, as it is written, 'and the night shines as the day' (Tehillim 139:12)."

paragraphs.text: Parallel: R. Tzvi Elimelech of Dinov, Bnei Yissaschar, Maamarei Chodesh Nisan, Maamar 4:5 — “It is stated in the Zohar: ‘The night shone like a day of the summer solstice, and all the people saw the judgment of the Holy One, blessed is He.’ One must consider what they saw. The very glory of His Name is the Name Havayah, which brings all being into existence and gives life to all from the beginning. This is the secret of ‘And God said, Let there be light’ at the beginning of the work of Creation, for the four fillings of Havayah equal 232, the number of yehi or. This is what the holy Zohar says, that the night shone: the secret of ‘Let there be light,’ for the light of this night was like that light.” Connection: Like Rav Tzadok, the Bnei Yissaschar identifies the light of the night of the Exodus in the Zohar with the light of “Let there be light”; he adds the numerical root, the four fillings of Havayah that equal yehi or.

paragraphs.text: Parallel: Sod Yesharim, First Night of Pesach 24 — “‘Leil, before she received the masculine’: when could this be? If Hashem removed His providence from His world even for a moment, all of creation would cease. But there is one point of the Holy One, blessed is He, that reaches constantly, and from it is all of creation’s existence; yet this point is very hidden, without creation’s knowledge; this is called ‘leil, before she received the masculine.’ For the main union is through knowledge (da'as), that it be recognized in creation’s knowledge that Hashem unites them… On this night Hashem illuminated da'as, letters of ‘edus,’ so a clear recognition was revealed that Hashem is always bound to Israel, and from this light of knowledge all the guarding is drawn to Israel.” Connection: The same Zohar on “leil” and “shimurim,” read here as the hidden point becoming known in da'as, which is the source of the night’s protection.

paragraphs.text: Zohar III 79b (Acharei Mos) — "Rabbi Shimon said: 'From one new moon to another and from one Shabbos to another' (Yeshayahu 66:23) — why are they weighed together? … The joy of one with the other is found only when Atika Kadisha is revealed… 'A psalm, a song for the Shabbos day' — then joy is found and the soul is increased, for Atika is revealed and the union is made ready."

paragraphs.text: Pesachim 85b — "Rav said in the name of Rabbi Chiya: An olive's bulk of the Pesach offering, and the Hallel splits the roofs." Rashi: the groups were so large that each received only an olive's bulk; and at the roar of the crowd reciting Hallel over the Pesach it seemed as if the roofs were splitting.
